title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 25
paragraphs: While Xerxes was doing these things, he had ropes prepared for the bridges as well, made of papyrus and of white flax, assigning this job to the Phoenicians and Egyptians. He was also making preparations to lay up provisions for his army along the march, so that neither the troops themselves nor the baggage animals would suffer shortage as they advanced into Greece. Having ascertained by inquiry which spots were most convenient, he ordered them to build the depots there, with supplies brought to various points by merchant ships and ferry-boats from all parts of Asia. They conveyed the greater part of the grain to the place in Thrace called Leuke Akte, others to Tyrodiza in the Perinthian territory, others to Doriscus, others to Eion on the Strymon, and others to Macedonia — the work divided among them.
